correctness.rationale: General proof: primitive chord-elimination cycles remove all free-length-n chord orbits from H_1(K_n,Z). In odd n the perimeter contributes a fixed Z; for even n the remaining antipodal chords plus perimeter have basis c,v_0,...,v_(h-1) and relation (s^h+1)v_0=c, giving the exact cyclic module Z[s]/((s-1)(s^h+1)), including its nonsplit index-two extension. Finite-field torus rational points follow from M/(q-s)M and normalization gives node- and branch-orbit zeta formulas. The Vandermonde model proves existence in every characteristic. The exact standalone checker verifies n=4..11, full unimodular change of basis and Frobenius action, plus separate extension-field point tests. Finite calculations are not treated as all-n proof.

value.rationale: A geometrically natural infinite family of nodal line divisors has a connected Picard torus whose integral Galois lattice is explicitly classifiable in every degree and characteristic. The parity-glued even-degree factor is a concrete index-two obstruction to using only rational representation theory, and changes the actual abstract rational-point group (notably in odd characteristic). The same proof identifies the exceptional Frobenius branch reversal affecting zeta functions; these are meaningful structural/arithmetic invariants beyond generic textbook normalization.
